findings.summary: The matcher fires on quoted mentions, so this job's own request, and every future root-cause request in this class, would be refused.
findings.evidence: request_words (reading.rs:3507) splits the whole request text and ignores quoting. The verbatim request of this job contains the line 'For any request that uses a figurative or structural term (ladder, layer, tier, publish, and similar)' and also 'Keep a glossary of project terms'. Athena writes root-cause requests like this one with introspection text quoted inside them. Under the plan, this job's own accepted reading has no 'Term ladder:', 'Term layer:' or 'Term tier:' line, so it would be refused. Every recurrence of this failure class would be refused the same way: the reader would have to define three words it only quotes and add a behaviour criterion for each. The reading's rule is 'each such word the request uses'. A word quoted as an example is a mention, not a use. Fix: Count only the words the request uses. One way: ignore the generated quote lines ('Introspection <id> (job <id>); prevention it proposed: ...', 'Cause: ...', 'Failure class: ...') and parenthesised example lists of the terms themselves. Keep plain request prose, so 7bf8 ('Use the ladder to decide ...') is still caught. Add a corpus accept case built from this job's own request with a reading that has no Term line, and add its input form to INPUT_FORMS. If you decide that mentions should count after all, say so in the doc and D164, and include them in the declared share.

findings.summary: The 3% estimate is unmeasured, and the plan ignores the in-loop replay, which does measure the share.
findings.evidence: The accepted reading says the dev must count the recorded requests that contain the words. The plan answers that records are absent from the producer snapshot. That is true per system facts, but the plan leaves the 3% unchecked until verification. A check does exist: run/mod.rs:2231-2250 (loop_replay) replays accepted readings inside the producer's loop, and producer.rs:49 (replay_problem) sends the measured count back when it is over the limit, which replay_limit_percent puts at 3+5=8%. 'ladder' and 'rung' are Athena's own project terms (athena_data::roles::Ladder, steward.rs, plan.rs), so stored Athena requests may hit the list more often than the estimate assumes. Fix: State that the in-loop replay is the measurement. If it sends the work back, the producer reports the measured share and either narrows the matcher or updates the declared figure in the doc, CHANGELOG and D164 to the measured value. Report the loop's figure in the final output instead of only 'no count possible'.
findings.location: Plan risks (first risk) and step 9 'no request count was possible'

findings.summary: The list includes terms the repository already defines (ladder, rung) and common code words (layer, tier); the doc should say these are refused too.
findings.evidence: 'ladder' and 'rung' already have a definition in the repository: docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md, the Ladder enum in athena-data, and steward.rs:12 'the requirements ladder'. 'layer' and 'tier' are common engineering words ('network layer', 'two-tier'). The check makes the reader restate a repo-defined term on every reading. The plan's open question covers growing the list, but it does not say whether a repo-defined term needs its own definition. Fix: Say in the doc comment and D164 that repo-defined project terms (the ladder and its rungs) are also refused until the reading restates them, and that this is part of the intended refusal rate. Alternatively, accept a 'Term ladder:' line that cites the defining file, so the reader repeats the meaning in a few words.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 term list; check_defined_terms doc limits

findings.summary: Several step cross-references in the dependents and demonstrations point to the wrong step.
findings.evidence: The briefs.rs test is 'updated in step 5', but briefs.rs is step 6. 'The rewritten replay test (step 6)' is step 5. Corpus cases 'added by plan step 6' are step 4. 'The doc is written in step 1' is step 2. Fix: Correct the step numbers so the producer follows the right step.

request_reading_mismatch: Partial narrowing. The request asks for a fix at the origin "so the whole class is prevented" (ambiguous-term-misread-as-narrow-deliverable). The reading turns that into a fixed list of four words (ladder, rung, tier, layer). Two of those words come from one cited job (7bf8), and the reading itself leaves job 0wtc (the "Hermes" term) outside the check. The plan follows the reading faithfully and says this in its doc, CHANGELOG and open question. The user accepted the reading, so this is noted here and not raised as a plan finding.
summary: I read reading.rs (refusing_check, request_words, check_outcome_state and its doc tests, replay_declaration and the replay limits), refusal_corpus.rs (CITED_REQUESTS, base_reading, with_behavior, INPUT_FORMS, the replay test), the READING_RULES test in briefs.rs, CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md and the steward/plan uses of ladder and rung. The plan's code claims hold. The step order is safe for both neighbour pin tests. request_words splits on '-' and keeps whole words. D163 is the last decision. The only readers of "are not caught", "outside the check" and "covers 1 of the 3" are the tests the plan updates. I found no existing test that sends a request containing one of the words through reading acceptance. Each demonstration runs the real gate and would fail without the behaviour. One soundness problem needs a revision. The matcher counts every occurrence of the word, including words quoted from cited introspections. Athena's own generated root-cause requests quote those words: the request of this very job contains "(ladder, layer, tier, publish, and similar)". Under the plan, this job's own accepted reading, and every future request in this failure class, would be refused unless it defined three words it only quotes. The other findings are minor: the plan does not say how its unmeasured 3% estimate will be checked, the word list includes two terms the repository already defines, and some step cross-references are wrong.
